rows.title: Refactor: remove unnecessary imports and redundant intermediate variables
rows.excerpt:
rollerTests.java` and `VetControllerTests.java` both had a class-level import for `MockMvcRequestBuilders` despite already having static imports for the individual methods (`get`, `post`) from the same class. This made the class-level import redundant and unused. Similarly, `OwnerController.java`, `PetController.java`, and `VisitController.java` each imported `java.util.Optional` which was only needed to hold an intermediate variable that was immediately unwrapped on the next line.

**Redundant intermediate variables** - In `OwnerController.java`, `PetController.java`, and `VisitController.java`, the pattern of assigning `owners.findById(...)` to an `optionalOwner` variable and then calling `.orElseThrow(...)` on the very next line served no purpose. SonarQube flags this under `java:S1488` - local variables should not be declared and then immediately returned or used.

## Changes
- Replaced `MockMvcRequestBuilders.post(...)` and `MockMvcRequestBuilders.get(...)` with the already-imported static equivalents in `OwnerControllerTests.java` and `VetControllerTests.java`, and removed the now-unused class-level imports
- Collapsed all `optionalOwner` intermediate variable declarations into single chained expressions using `.orElseThrow(...)` directly on the repository call in `OwnerController.java`, `PetController.java`, and `VisitController.java`
- Removed the `java.util.Optional` import from each controller where it was no longer referenced

## Sustainability Impact
Redundant code and unnecessary imports increase the noise developers must read through when understanding or modifying a file. Unused imports can mislead future contributors into thinking a type is meaningfully used, and they accumulate silently over time if not caught early.

## Files Changed
- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/OwnerController.java`
- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/PetController.java`
- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/VisitController.java`
- `src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/OwnerControllerTests.java`
- `src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/VetControllerTests.java`

rows.title: Documentation: Improve documentation across classes
rows.excerpt:
s in the owner and vet areas were under-documented. While the code was functional, the intent of the domain objects and controller flows was not immediately clear to readers, especially around model preparation, pet ownership rules, and veterinarian specialty handling.

The `Owner` domain model, `PetController`, and `Vet` model each contain logic that benefits from clearer class-level and method-level documentation. Without that context, future contributors have to infer behavior from implementation details rather than from the API contract.

## Changes
- Expanded the class-level documentation in `Owner.java` to explain its role as the core owner entity and its relationship to pets
- Added method-level documentation in `PetController.java` to clarify:
  - model attribute preparation
  - request binding
  - validation flow
  - pet create/update handling
- Improved the class and method documentation in `Vet.java` to explain:
  - specialty management
  - the read-only sorted view exposed to callers

## Sustainability Impact
Better documentation reduces cognitive load for future maintenance work. These classes are part of the main application flow, so clearer comments and Javadoc help new contributors understand why the code exists, not just what it does.

This improves long-term maintainability by:
- reducing onboarding friction for new contributors
- making controller and domain behavior easier to reason about
- lowering the risk of incorrect future modifications
- improving overall code readability and maintainability

## Files Changed
- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/Owner.java`
- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/PetController.java`
- `src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/Vet.java`

on `(owner_id, name)`.
   - **MySQL**: Add a unique constraint `UNIQUE (owner_id, name)`.
   - **PostgreSQL**: Add a unique functional index: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX unique_owner_pet_name ON pets (owner_id, LOWER(name));`.
2. **Immediate Persistence**:
   - Change `save()` to `saveAndFlush()` in [PetController.java](file:///Users/spring-petclinic/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/PetController.java) to ensure SQL execution and trigger constraint violations within the try-catch block.
3. **Graceful Exception Translation**:
   - Update [PetController.java](file:///Users/spring-petclinic/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/PetController.java) to catch `DataIntegrityViolationException`, verify if it is the specific `unique_owner_pet_name` violation, and translate it into a clean validation error on the name field.

NOTE: To preserve the existing application behavior, the database constraints are implemented in a case-insensitive manner, matching the current Java validation (`equalsIgnoreCase()`).


## Testing
- **Unit Tests**: Added mock exception handling tests in [PetControllerTests.java](file:///Users/spring-petclinic/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/PetControllerTests.java) for both create and edit flows.
- **Service Integration Tests**: Added test cases in [ClinicServiceTests.java](file:///Users/spring-petclinic/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/ClinicServiceTests.java) to verify that duplicate pet name insertions fail with a `DataIntegrityViolationException` and that same pet names under different owners succeed.
- **Automated Concurrency Test**: Created [PetClinicConcurrencyTests.java](file:///Users/spring-petclinic/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/PetClinicConcurrencyTests.java) executing concurrent requests in parallel. The test verifies that only one request succeeds and the other is rejected with a validation error.

## Scope
This change is tightly scoped to the `Pet` uniqueness invariant, leaving all other entities and system configurations untouched.
